## Why This Is Asked
Tests pragmatic KCA design for distributed, latency-sensitive fintech workloads with real-world constraints (two regions, Kubernetes, SPIFFE IDs, short cert lifetimes).

## Key Concepts
- KCA workflow for microservices across regions
- OPA-based dynamic policy
- PQC crypto agility and fallback
- Container image attestation and SPIFFE binding
- Cross-region trust anchors, revocation, auditing
- Rollout and failover testing in prod-like scenarios

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-policy snippet illustrating per-service scope gate
const policy = `package kca
default allow = false
allow {
  input.spiffe_id.startsWith("spiffe://cluster.trade/")
  input.scope == "trade"
}`
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle PKI lifecycle when a region is isolated for hours?
- What metrics and dashboards would you surface for attestation success rates and revocation latency?

## Why This Is Asked

Evaluates KCA design expertise across hybrid real-time data pipelines, focusing on cross-region trust establishment, policy propagation mechanisms, and revocation strategies while maintaining low-latency TLS handshakes under bursty ingestion scenarios.

## Key Concepts

- Hardware attestation and root of trust at edge collectors
- Regional bootstrap and central KCA integration
- SPIFFE IDs per tenant and service-scoped certificates
- Policy bundles with 1-minute renewal cycles
- Crypto agility and online/offline revocation
- OCSP/CRLs and comprehensive audit logging

## Critical Success Factors

- Sub-300ms certificate issuance under bursty ingestion
- Clock skew tolerance across hybrid infrastructure
- Seamless certificate rotation without data loss
- Zero-trust enforcement across on-prem to cloud boundaries

- Token-based enrollment

```javascript
function enroll(token, tenantId){

  if(!consumeQuota(tenantId, 1)) throw 'quota exceeded'

}
```
